## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Two Important defects need fixing first. Titles with accented or non-Latin letters come out mangled or empty because the slug pattern only keeps ASCII. The PR description also leaves out the `## Testing` section that `AGENTS.md` requires. This review read `AGENTS.md`, the PR title and body, the full diff, and both added files, and traced `slugify` against the four parametrized test cases by reading them; it ran no tests. Both new modules open with a docstring that says what they are for, as `AGENTS.md:3` requires.

## Changes
The PR adds `app/slug.py` with a `slugify(title)` helper that lowercases the title, collapses runs of characters outside `[a-z0-9]` into one hyphen, and trims hyphens from the ends. It also adds parametrized tests in `tests/test_slug.py`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/slug.py:13 — correctness — Keep non-ASCII letters or transliterate before slugging — `slugify("Café Menu")` returns `"caf-menu"` and `slugify("日本語")` returns `""`, because `[^a-z0-9]+` treats every non-ASCII letter as a separator. The PR body says the function replaces "runs of non-alphanumeric characters", but `é` and `日` are alphanumeric (`"é".isalnum()` is `True`) and still get stripped. None of the tests in `tests/test_slug.py` uses a non-ASCII title, so nothing catches this. — Pages with accented titles get truncated URLs. Pages whose titles use no Latin letters all get the same empty slug, so their URLs collide or come out blank. — Fix: Either normalize with `unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", ...)` and drop combining marks before the ASCII substitution, or use `re.sub(r"[\W_]+", "-", title.lower())` to keep Unicode word characters. Add a non-ASCII case to the parametrized tests for whichever behavior you choose.
- PR body — correctness — Add the required `## Testing` section to the description — The description has no `## Testing` section, which breaks the rule at `AGENTS.md:4`: "Every pull-request description has a `## Testing` section that says how the change was verified." The body is one sentence describing what `slugify` does. — Reviewers and maintainers get no record of how the change was verified, which the project policy requires.

(none)
